implementation: phase4-coordinator/internal/trustpool/durable_store.go:func verifyManifestAcceptanceState(ctx context.Context, q eventQueryer, events []DurableEvent) error

gap.rationale: Pool lifecycle/migration/failover reconstruction now includes local coordinator-store wiring for accepted manifest verdict evidence: migration creates/backfills projection and high-water tables once behind a durable completion marker, append/promote paths verify projection state before mutation and after projection writes, reconstruction and later store opens verify event/projection/high-water consistency in one transaction, and malformed replay clears routeable snapshots through the registry disable path. Local restrictive lifecycle admin control is wired through the same validated durable event path: paused/draining/retired transitions survive replay, refresh the live registry, active remains promotion-only, and paused candidate pools can reactivate only through PromotePool after local activation preflight. Signed emergency controls now bind the latest manifest, signer set, operation id, action, validity window, and optional target provider; pause/drain/retire append proof-bearing lifecycle events, while `revoke_immediate` appends proof-bearing durable revocation, advances the route-generation fence, and cancels active uncommitted dispatch attempts. Pool-selected provider dispatch now atomically re-checks routeability/generation while recording a live delivery counter at the provider-dispatched boundary; stale final dispatch fails with retryable `pool_state_stale` before provider relay, routeable snapshot reloads preserve that counter, and local/signed `retired` controls fail closed unless the pool is already non-routeable and the counter is drained, forcing active pools through `draining` before retirement. Still pending: production migration evidence, tamper-evident full rollback protection, full delegation/lifecycle reconstruction, signed journey evidence, production activation evidence, and 0 C/H/M launch audit.

Manifest authority + signer-set key lifecycle: slice 2 (v0.0.9) implements policy-core signature verification against a signer set; slice 3 (v0.0.10) implements the append-only, hash-chained AUTHORITY LOG that establishes/versions those signer sets and sets their revocation state - the authority-log-entry content byte grammar + hash + signing preimage, and BuildAuthorityLog chain-replay verification (structural signer-set validation, strictly-monotonic signer_set_version/rollback reject, prev-hash chain, revokes_versions prior-existing-only, and authorization by one root-issuer signature or M-of-N of a prior still-authorized lower-versioned set), materializing signer_set_version -> SignerSet for policy-core verification - frozen by golden vectors (genesis->rotate->revoke). Slice 5 (v0.0.12) adds verdict-replay reconstruction (ReconstructPool in persist.go): a recorded acceptance verdict is replayed on restart rather than re-evaluated against the current wall-clock, grandfathering a policy accepted before its signer set was later revoked. Signed emergency control messages now verify against the manifest authority root or current operational signer set, bind latest accepted manifest version/digest, and for `revoke_immediate` bind the target provider identity. Still deferred: operator-provenance binding, root-issuer-compromise supersedes lineage, and production signed evidence.
